Anatomy of schema.prisma

Two configuration blocks that sit above every model: which client to generate, and which database to talk to.

Every schema.prisma file opens with two configuration blocks, before any actual data model appears. Figure 2.4 is the top of this project's file.

// Figure 2.4: schema configuration (prisma/schema.prisma, excerpt)
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "mysql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}
  • generator client tells Prisma what to generate from this schema — here, a JavaScript client (there are other generators for other languages/ targets, not used in this project).
  • datasource db tells Prisma which database engine the schema targets (mysql — this affects what column types and SQL get generated) and where to find it — env("DATABASE_URL") reads the connection string from .env, the previous topic, rather than hardcoding it here. This is the only place in the whole schema file that mentions environment variables or connection details at all; everything below it is just the shape of your data.

Everything from here on in the file is a model block — one per table, which is where the actual ticketing domain gets described.
